page0.text:
Meet up with Tohsaka.
She told me to withdraw now.
If I'm going to refuse and fight, I need to let her know.
That I won't withdraw on my own, and that we're still cooperating.
And...

page1.text:
I can't let her fight by herself.
I owe her big time.
I can't step down until I repay her for that.

page2.text:
"...And she always screws up at the most crucial moment... She's so unreliable, I can't let her be alone."
I adjust the bag on my shoulder.
...I'm aware that I won't be of much help and that she will object.
But I can't obtain peace of mind until I see Tohsaka's face.

page3.text:
...This is hypothetical, but...
If she gets hurt without me knowing, I can't even be there to help her...

page4.text:
"...Phew."
I sit down on a bench and rest my burning body.
It's past noon.
I've searched all around Shinto, but I haven't found anything.

page5.text:
"...Damn. I knew it wasn't going to be easy, but I didn't think I would find nothing."
I knew that I had no way to find Tohsaka from the start.
I tested my luck and looked around town, but I couldn't find her or even traces of her.

page6.text:
"...The other Masters aren't coming out either... I guess there's no need to even attack me now that I don't have a Command Spell."
I take a deep breath and lean back on the backrest.

page7.text:
...
I won't get anywhere like this.
Tohsaka isn't naïve enough to show her tail, and my last resort to use myself as decoy to lure other Masters is failing so far.

page8.text:
...I get a bit uneasy.
I can't find Tohsaka and can't save Saber.
They might already be in an irreparable situation by the time I find them...

page9.text:
"...It's still noon. I won't let that happen so easily."
I stand up from the bench.
I ignore my left shoulder that starts heating up again and leave the park.
